chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “If two men bring a case before you, then do not judge for the first until you hear from the other, for when you do that, the judgment will become clear to you.”
ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “So I continued thereafter as a judge.” And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him: “O Allah, grant him understanding of judgment.”

key_terms.الْآخَرِ: the other litigant or opposing party
key_terms.تَقَاضَى: to bring a dispute or legal case for judgment
key_terms.تَقْضِ: to judge or issue a ruling

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about hearing both sides before making a judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the judicial principle that a judge must hear both sides before issuing a ruling. It also highlights the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم prayer for Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام to be granted understanding in judgment, showing both procedural justice and divinely aided discernment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3238 - It is narrated from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) that Imam (as) said:

The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"If two men bring a case before you, do not judge in favor of the first until you hear from the other, for if you do so, the judgment will become clear to you."

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "After that, I continued to serve as a judge."
And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: "O Allah (swt), grant him understanding in judgment."
